content:
For years, Canada was the first choice for many students from Kerala. Today, rising Canada tuition fees for Indian students, higher proof-of-funds rules and a cap on study permits mean the decision needs much more careful planning. Whether you are preparing for IELTS, PTE or TOEFL, this guide explains why studying in Canada costs more now, what the changes mean for your English test plans, and which alternatives are worth a look.

How much has tuition in Canada gone up?

Statistics Canada publishes average tuition fees every year. Its figures show that the average annual undergraduate tuition for international students in Canada has risen from about CAD 23,700 in 2016/2017 to about CAD 42,100 in 2026/2027. Over the same period, international students have come to pay several times what Canadian students pay for the same degree.

Average annual tuition, 2026/2027 (Statistics Canada) Approx. amount
International undergraduate CAD 42,100
International graduate CAD 24,700
Canadian undergraduate (for comparison) CAD 8,000

These are national averages. Fees vary a great deal by province, institution and course. Ontario has the highest average international undergraduate tuition, at around CAD 50,000 a year, while some Atlantic provinces are far lower. Professional programmes such as engineering, business and medicine usually cost more than arts or general science. Always check the exact fee on your institution’s website.

Tuition is only part of the bill. Accommodation, food, transport, health insurance and course materials add significantly to the yearly cost, particularly in large cities such as Toronto and Vancouver where rents are high.

Why are Canada tuition fees for Indian students rising?

Universities rely on international fees

Many Canadian colleges and universities have come to depend on international students to balance their budgets, as government funding has not kept pace with their costs. In many provinces, fees for international students are not regulated in the same way as fees for Canadian students, so institutions have more freedom to raise them.

Inflation and operating costs

Higher salaries, building maintenance, technology and general inflation have all increased the cost of running institutions, and part of that cost is passed on through tuition.

Fewer study permits

Since 2024 the Canadian government has capped the number of study permits it issues. With fewer international students, some institutions face financial pressure, which can affect both fees and the range of programmes on offer.

Other changes that raise the cost of studying in Canada

  • Higher proof of funds: study permit applicants must show they can cover living costs in addition to tuition and travel. IRCC raised this amount from CAD 10,000 to CAD 20,635 for a single applicant in January 2024, then to CAD 22,895 from September 2025, and it now reviews the figure every year. Check the current amount on the IRCC website before you apply.
  • End of the Student Direct Stream: the SDS, which many Indian students used for faster processing, closed on 8 November 2024. Applications now go through the regular study permit process.
  • Provincial attestation letters: most new students need a letter from the province or territory where they will study, which counts towards that province’s share of the cap. IRCC has exempted some groups, including master’s and doctoral students at public institutions from January 2026.

Rules like these change often, so rely on the official IRCC website rather than old social media posts. Our article on the global decline in study and work visas gives more background.

What this means for IELTS, PTE and TOEFL aspirants

A strong score matters more than ever

With fewer places and closer scrutiny of applications, a comfortable English test score helps you meet admission requirements without delays. A strong score can also matter for some scholarships, so aim above the minimum where you can.

Choose the right test for your goal

  • For university admission in Canada: most institutions accept IELTS Academic, and many also accept PTE Academic and TOEFL iBT. Check your institution’s list and minimum scores.
  • For permanent residence through Express Entry: IRCC accepts CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training and PTE Core for English. IELTS Academic, PTE Academic and TOEFL are not accepted for Express Entry.
  • If you are keeping other countries open: IELTS is accepted across most popular destinations, which keeps your options flexible while you decide. Our comparison of PTE and IELTS can help you choose.

Plan your test date around your budget decision

If you are unsure whether you can afford Canada, take your English test early anyway. A valid score lets you apply quickly to Canada or an alternative destination once your finances are clear.

Alternatives to Canada worth considering

If costs in Canada are beyond your budget, these destinations are popular with Indian students. Fees, visa rules and work rights change, so check official sources for each.

  • Germany: most public universities charge little or no tuition for many programmes, though some states charge non-EU students fees and you must still show funds for living costs. Many programmes are taught in English at master’s level.
  • Ireland: an English-speaking country with many one-year master’s programmes, which can reduce the total cost of study.
  • New Zealand: a smaller, welcoming study destination where fees at some institutions can compare well with Canada.
  • France and the Netherlands: a growing number of English-taught programmes, with scholarships available at many institutions.

Most universities in these countries accept IELTS, and many also accept PTE Academic or TOEFL iBT, so the English test you prepare for now remains useful wherever you go.

How to plan if you still want to study in Canada

  1. Budget for the full cost: include tuition, living costs, health insurance, travel and the proof of funds, not just the first-year fee.
  2. Compare provinces and institutions: fees outside the most expensive provinces and big cities can be considerably lower.
  3. Look for scholarships early: many awards have deadlines well before admission deadlines.
  4. Plan education loans carefully: understand the repayment terms and interest before you commit.
  5. Check work rules from official sources: do not build your budget on assumptions about part-time income.
  6. Prepare your English test in good time: a strong score avoids last-minute retakes and missed intakes.

Frequently asked questions

Is Canada still a good option for Indian students?

It can be, if you plan your finances carefully and choose your institution and programme wisely. Canada still offers well-regarded education, but the higher tuition, proof of funds and study permit cap mean you should compare it honestly with other destinations.

Which English test should I take for Canada?

For admission, check what your institution accepts: most accept IELTS Academic and many accept PTE Academic and TOEFL iBT. For permanent residence through Express Entry, you need an approved test such as IELTS General Training, CELPIP-General or PTE Core.

Will my IELTS score work for other countries if I change my plans?

IELTS is accepted in most popular study destinations, including the UK, Ireland, Australia and New Zealand, and by many universities in Europe. Check the type of IELTS (Academic or General Training) and the minimum score required for each university or visa.
